production_changes.change: Inner origin dispatch is allowed only for http, https or file. Nested blob and inner ftp/ws/wss now produce opaque origins instead of the former recursive tuple-origin path.
production_changes.precision: The free function still calls url_origin for the three permitted terminal schemes, so source wording should describe bounded dispatch rather than claiming that this call disappears. Those permitted schemes do not enter the blob branch.

production_changes.change: The path encode set now includes ^, and inherited path-segment sets encode it as %5E. Userinfo already encoded this character. Query and special-query character sets are unchanged.
production_changes.implication: Serialization of paths containing a literal caret changes; checks that rely on exact serialized URL text should account for that input class.

production_changes.change: Remove the code that discarded the parsed hostname when a file URL path began with a Windows drive letter. The host and host boundary are retained.
production_changes.implication: This affects file URL parsing with a host and drive-letter path, independent of which platform parses the URL.

production_changes.change: For Context::UrlParser, a backslash terminates the port only for schemes with a default port; a non-special scheme returns InvalidPort instead. The existing delimiter treatment for HTTP-family/default-port schemes remains.
production_changes.implication: Malformed non-special URLs previously accepted with a backslash at that position are rejected. This branch-specific change should not be generalized to every setter.

production_changes.change: Search for the prior slash only within the path rather than across the scheme and authority. Keep explicit guards for a root/empty path and the Windows drive-letter slash.
production_changes.assessment: Source review supports the stated normalization equivalence while eliminating repeated scans through a long authority. The empty file-root setter case is guarded before slicing. No timing or runtime claim is made by this review.

production_changes.change: Serializer::for_suffix clamps an oversized start_position to the target length instead of panicking. Its signature and the rest of the form parser/serializer body are unchanged in this release diff.
production_changes.implication: Valid offsets keep the same logic; invalid oversized offsets now append from the end of the target. No general form-encoding table change was found.

other_changes.assessment: next_utf8 uses Option propagation in place of an equivalent match, and selection of a file base uses Option::filter in place of equivalent and_then logic. No additional behavioral difference was found in these local simplifications.

other_changes.area: URL library and path-segment source files
other_changes.assessment: Remaining changes are documentation/reference fixes, including the displayed documentation version and file in the documented special-scheme list.

IDNA source edits are comments/documentation; Unicode18 data changes are tests. percent_encoding removes two unnecessary clones, but the authorized two-package Cargo delta does not import that monorepo source edit if the existing percent-encoding registry version/checksum remains unchanged.

The remaining diff updates upstream tests, WPT data/expected failures, a benchmark, CI compatibility pins and funding configuration. Their presence is not evidence that these tests were run for this task.

data.advisory_context: RUSTSEC-2026-0592; url 2.5.8 nested-blob origin recursion. Canonical advisory and patched-dependency verification are owned by separate evidence records.
data.scope: Read-only Auth and Issuance Url::origin caller reachability review, with only the immediate HTTP/transport callers and origin policy needed to establish input boundaries.

inspected_dependency_source.observed_behavior: url_origin matches the blob scheme, parses url.path(), and recursively calls url_origin on the parsed inner URL. The observation is source inspection only.

findings.input: Caller-controlled redirect_uri accepted by the login/register query and retained in PkceState.
flow: HTTP initiate sanitizes redirect_uri and passes it into the application login/registration command.
For a foreign scheme, sanitize_redirect_uri returns parsed.path(); the path of a nested blob URL can itself remain a blob URL.
After a successful OIDC callback, the HTTP callback handler calls build_ui_redirect_url with the retained redirect.
resolve_post_auth_redirect sanitizes again and, when the result is not '/', evaluates is_same_origin_root.
is_same_origin_root evaluates authority_url(&url), which calls Url::origin(), before its later path, query and fragment checks.
findings.authentication_precondition: The reviewed callback origin call occurs only after state.application.callback returns a successful result and the callback's session handling succeeds. Error callbacks return earlier. This is not a claim of an unauthenticated direct crash path.
findings.guards: UiOriginPolicy normalizes the configured base to HTTP(S); sanitize_redirect_uri rejects protocol-relative input and checks scheme equality before its own same-origin branch. Those checks do not guarantee that its foreign-scheme path fallback is relative.
findings.route_size_limit: No redirect_uri length check is present in the reviewed login/register initiate function. Global proxy/server/request-target and storage limits were not assessed.
findings.interpretation: A sufficiently nested blob URL can survive the sanitizer passes and reach the affected origin computation. Static reachability is established; stack exhaustion, practical payload limits and an end-to-end exploit were not executed or measured.

findings.flow: The application restricts the callback URL to HTTP(S) without user information, then callback.join(redirect_uri) may replace its scheme. It calls redirect.origin() for equality before rechecking the joined URL's scheme.
actual_http_guards: redirect_uri length must not exceed 2048 bytes
exactly one matching application Origin header
session cookie and successful session validation
the badge/email branch requires a recent server-created session within 300 seconds; sessions with OIDC enrollment hints take the separate authorization branch
findings.interpretation: The callback scheme check alone does not constrain an absolute joined redirect. The HTTP route's explicit length and authentication guards remain material; this review does not claim the bounded route reaches a stack-overflow threshold.

controls: External OIDC endpoint/allowlist URLs pass external_https_url (HTTPS, host and userinfo/fragment checks, plus endpoint size/control-character checks) before origin is evaluated.
The internal JWKS-discovery path rejects a discovered non-HTTP(S) scheme before comparing origins.
OIDC provider construction validates configuration; configured issuers are normalized as HTTP(S), or exact HTTPS in external-provider mode.
UiOriginPolicy normalize_origin rejects non-HTTP(S), missing host and userinfo before calling origin.
findings.interpretation: No nested-blob origin reachability was found through these reviewed OIDC and UI-origin paths.

findings.low_level_order: SecureExternalEvidenceTransport::send computes request.url.origin before calling prepare. OutboundHttpClient::send compares or serializes url.origin before its downstream origin policy validation. Their request types do not themselves encode a scheme restriction.
findings.production_input_flow: The reviewed template executor renders the URL, calls validate_api_url, then only appends query parameters before constructing ExternalEvidenceHttpRequest and invoking the transport.
preceding_template_guards: scheme must be HTTP or HTTPS
findings.constructor_scope: The scoped source search found this production ExternalEvidenceHttpRequest constructor; other direct request/client constructions found in the reviewed modules were test code.
findings.interpretation: The reviewed production template path rejects blob before either low-level origin computation. Direct internal callers of the public request/transport interface could bypass that validation, so the lower-level API is not intrinsically safe for arbitrary Url values.
